                                         Document understanding is a long-standing practi-                 fonts. Traditional document question answering meth-
                                         cal task. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have grad-                ods usually employ OCR-based pipelines [29, 36]
                                         ually become a primary approach in this domain,                   to extract textual content and then feed it into large
                                         demonstrating effective performance on single-page                language models (LLMs) for response generation.
                                         tasks. However, their effectiveness diminishes when               However, such approaches often lose critical multi-
                                         handling long documents. In such scenarios, clues are             modal cues, leading to imperfect and shallow doc-

                                         relevant content, the retrieved results still contain             capabilities, particularly in single-page document un-
                                         substantial redundancy. To address these limitations,             derstanding [20–22, 58]. Nevertheless, their ability to
                                         we propose SLEUTH, a multi-agent framework. Con-                  comprehend long-context documents remains uncer-
                                         cretely, SLEUTH orchestrates a retriever and four                 tain [31, 57, 59]. Long documents introduce extensive
                                         collaborative agents in a coarse-to-fine process. The             contexts where most information is redundant, while
                                         framework identifies key textual and visual clues                 the key evidence required to answer a query is often
                                         within the retrieved pages, filters for salient visual ev-        sparse and scattered across multiple pages and modali-
                                         idence such as tables and charts, and analyzes the                ties. This characteristic poses substantial challenges to
                                         query to devise a reasoning strategy. It ultimately syn-          existing VLMs. The core objective of long-document
                                         thesizes a distilled, evidence-dense multimodal con-              understanding lies in precisely locating informative
                                         text to generate the final prediction. SLEUTH is                  evidence from massive content and organizing it into a
                                         model-agnostic and scalable. When paired with ad-                 high-quality contextual representation suitable for rea-
                                         vanced VLM backbones, it consistently improves per-               soning and response generation.

Figure 2. Overall Framework. SLEUTH adopts a coarse-to-fine pipeline: (1) a visual retriever selects Top-K pages; (2) Clue
Discovery Agent records and refines evidence, Page Screening Agent filters irrelevant page images, (3) Difficulty Assessment
Agent analyzes query complexity, and (4) Core Decision Agent reasons over the distilled, evidence-dense context.

Figure 4. Case study. Compared with basic methods that rely solely on direct input of the top-5 retrieved pages, SLEUTH per-
forms dynamic correction through multi-step evidence recording and page-wise filtering, effectively preventing hallucination
accumulation caused by multimodal long-context inputs with complex layouts inputs.

tions and multi-backbone evaluations demonstrate its                             nal right answer. The collaborative cooperation among
universality and flexibility.                                                    the various agents in this process achieves redun-
Visual vs. Multimodal Retrieval Input. To verify                                 dancy elimination, preserves key clues, and over-
whether purely visual page evidence is more advan-                               comes hallucination interference. This example high-

We employed one agent to process the Top-5 visual                                even in dense, noisy long document environments.
pages retrieved by ColPali. Simultaneously, we de-
ployed a second agent to process the Top-5 text pages.                           5. Conclusion
We obtained these text pages by extracting content via
MinerU2.5 [23] and retrieving them with BGE M3.                                  This paper presents SLEUTH, a framework that re-
Both agents extracted evidence using the same prompt                             examines long-document question answering from the
logic. Finally, we merged the evidence sets from both                            perspective of context engineering. Without modify-
the visual and textual agents for the subsequent rea-                            ing model architectures, SLEUTH organizes contex-
soning process. As shown in Table 4, using purely                                tual inputs to improve the utilization of long con-
visual page inputs yields higher average accuracy on                             texts and maintain stable reasoning. Through a coarse-
both benchmarks, outperforming the multimodal input                              to-fine process that narrows the search space and
setting by +2.58% and +2.34% points, respectively.                               constructs evidence-focused multimodal contexts, it
This result supports our hypothesis that visual pages                            achieves better document understanding while pre-
serve as a highly compressed and structure-preserving                            serving interpretability. Experiments show consistent
unified representation. It also aligns with recent works                         gains across benchmarks, demonstrating the effective-
such as DeepSeek-OCR [37], which advocate for uni-                               ness of context engineering for long-document tasks.
fied visual input as an effective means of compressing                               Despite promising results, we identify two primary
long contexts. More analysis of the ablation experi-                             limitations. First, the framework relies heavily on the
ments can be found in the Appendix C.                                            initial retriever. If critical pages are missed early on,
                                                                                 downstream agents cannot recover them. Second, the
                                                                                 purely prompt-driven design limits the system’s abil-
4.4. Qualitative Analysis
                                                                                 ity to self-evolve through experience. To address these
Figure 4 illustrates how SLEUTH alleviates hallu-                                issues, our future work will focus on three directions.
cination caused by redundant long-document inputs.                               First, we will introduce feedback-based retrieval to re-
When asked questions, the base method directly feeds                             duce dependency on a single step. Second, we will
all retrieved pages to the VLM, where excessive nu-                              integrate Reinforcement Learning and external toolk-
merical noise confuses the model and yields incor-                               its for autonomous optimization. Furthermore, we will
rect answers. In contrast, SLEUTH builds evidence                                integrate existing methods for enhancing reasoning
page-wise with self-corrective reasoning: the Clue                               capabilities with techniques for improving retrieval
Discovery Agent reads each retrieved page holisti-                               precision to further advance the document understand-
cally and writes structured clues; the Page Screen-                              ing capabilities of AI. Third, we will extend the frame-
ing Agent prunes visually irrelevant pages; and the                              work to support multilingual and handwritten docu-
Core Decision Agent fuses the clues to produce the fi-                           ments to verify its broader generalization capabilities.

C.2. Visual vs. Multimodal Retrieval Input                       sion—work sequentially to extract structured clues,
                                                                 filter visual noise, perceive task difficulty, and synthe-
To verify whether purely visual page evidence is                 size final reasoning. This coarse-to-fine design works
more advantageous for our architecture, we compare               on short and fixed-length inputs during evidence ex-
a visual-only setting with a multimodal setting. In              traction and screening, which makes it easier to iden-
the visual-only setting, the Clue Discovery Agent di-            tify useful information and suppress noise. The final
rectly processes the top-K pages returned by the vi-             reasoning then operates on a concise yet evidence-
sual retriever (ColPali-v1.3 [11]). In the multimodal            dense structured context that adapts to each query, en-
setting, there are two independent retrieval streams:            abling more accurate and focused understanding.
a visual stream (as above) and a textual stream. For                 Empirical results across four benchmarks demon-
the textual stream, we extract page-level text with              strate clear advantages of SLEUTH over strong RAG-
MinerU 2.5 [23] and perform textual retrieval with               based and agent-based baselines. Its training-free
BGE M3 [3]. The Clue Discovery Agent prompt is                   and model-agnostic design allows consistent improve-
minimally adjusted so that, when handling text-based             ment under different backbones. Notably, visual-only
pages, it reads the extracted text blocks using the same         page inputs outperform multimodal retrieval, suggest-
evidence format. Each stream independently selects               ing that visual layouts inherently preserve document
its own top-5 results, and both are then passed to sub-          structure and reasoning cues. Through these findings,
sequent agents, thereby constructing the data flow for           SLEUTH establishes a new paradigm and emphasizes
the multimodal retrieval setting.                                that context quality is the key factor determining the
                                                                 effectiveness of long-document understanding.

performance. We speculate that two factual properties            agents cannot compensate. Incorporating feedback-
of visual pages are relevant here. First, visual pages           based or hierarchical retrieval may mitigate this de-
naturally provide a more compact representation: their           pendency. The binary difficulty estimation is efficient
spatial layout organizes information in place and re-            but coarse, which may not capture intermediate rea-
duces redundancy. Second, the visual modality offers             soning cases. Extending it to a continuous scale or
a unified representation: text, tables, and charts are en-       adopting a light expert-routing strategy could improve
coded in the same image form. This uniform form pre-             adaptability. Moreover, current experiments focus on
serves layout relations and visible cues, which helps            English administrative and academic documents, leav-

  You are a Detective, an expert evidence col-         tions.
  lector for document question answering. Your         Your task is to examine this PDF page image
  task is to carefully examine the given PDF           and determine:
  page and extract ALL evidence that might be          1. Whether there are any charts, figures, ta-
  relevant to answering the question.                      bles, or diagrams on this page.
  Question: {question}                                 2. If charts/figures/tables exist, whether they
  Page Information:                                        are relevant to answering the given ques-
  • Page Number: {page num}                                tion.
  Your Task:                                           Question: {question}
  1. Carefully examine the page image!                 Page Number: {page number}
  2. Identify ALL facts, data points, and infor-       Instructions:
     mation that could help answer the question.       1. First, carefully examine the page image to
  3. Extract specific evidence with:                       identify any visual elements like:
     • Exact quotes or data values                         • Charts (bar charts, line charts, pie charts,
     • Context where information appears                      etc.)
     • Explanation of why it’s relevant                    • Figures (diagrams, illustrations, photos,
  Output Format: Provide your analysis in the                 etc.)
  following JSON format:                                   • Tables (data tables, comparison tables,
                                                              etc.)
  { "page number": {page num},                             • Infographics or other data visualizations
     "has relevant evidence":                          2. If you find charts/figures/tables, assess
  true/false,                                              their relevance to the question:
     "evidence items": [ {                                 • Completely Relevant: Directly contains
    "evidence type":                                          information needed to answer the ques-
  "text/chart/table/figure",                                  tion.
     "content": "The actual                                • Relevant: Might contain related infor-
  evidence (quote, data, or                                   mation, but relevance is uncertain.
  description)",                                           • Irrelevant: The chart/figure/table exists
     "location": "Description of                              but is clearly unrelated to the question.
  where this appears on the                            3. If there are NO charts/figures/tables on this
  page",                                                   page (only pure text), output ”none”.
     "relevance": "Explanation                         Output Format (strictly follow this format):
  of why this is relevant...",                         Has Chart: [Yes/No]
     "confidence":                                     Relevance: [Completely Relevant/ Relevant/
  "high/medium/low" } ],                               Irrelevant]

  important insights or patterns
  noticed" }

  Important Guidelines:
  • Be thorough - collect ALL potentially rele-
    vant evidence.
  • Include exact numbers, percentages, and
    specific facts.
  • Note relationships between data points.
  • If the page is not relevant, explain why!
  • Please think carefully and avoid generating
    content that does not conform to reality.
  Now examine the page and provide your evi-
  dence collection in valid JSON format.
